container.title: Application / Docker Container
container.summary: Lightweight, standalone execution environment packaging application code, libraries, runtime, and configuration.
container.details: Containers encapsulate the microservice application so it runs consistently across local development, staging, and production environments. In this architecture, containers run your core backend API and background tasks.
container.architectureRole: Packaged as a Docker image, pushed to Amazon ECR, and orchestrated across servers using Amazon ECS.

ecr.title: Amazon ECR (Elastic Container Registry)
ecr.summary: Fully managed, secure container image registry for storing, managing, and deploying Docker images.
ecr.details:
ECR provides encrypted storage, image scanning for CVE vulnerabilities, and high availability. It integrates natively with ECS and EKS for automated zero-downtime deployment pipelines.

• Best for: Version controlling application builds and securely passing images to deployment tools.
• The Catch: It is strictly storage; pushing an image to ECR does nothing until a compute service like ECS pulls and executes it.
ecr.architectureRole: Receives container builds from CI/CD and acts as the secure source repository from which ECS pulls images.

ecs.title: Amazon ECS (Elastic Container Service)
ecs.summary: Highly scalable container management and orchestration service that schedules and maintains Docker containers.
ecs.details:
If a container crashes or becomes unhealthy, ECS automatically terminates and restarts it to maintain desired task counts.

Launch Types:
1. EC2 Launch Type: ECS places and manages containers on virtual machine instances that you provision, configure, and maintain.
2. AWS Fargate (Serverless): AWS completely provisions and manages the underlying servers; you only pay for the exact CPU and memory consumed by each container.
ecs.architectureRole: Executes backend container tasks behind the Application Load Balancer and interacts with RDS, ElastiCache, and SQS.

rds.title: Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service)
rds.summary: Managed relational database engine supporting PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, and Amazon Aurora.
rds.details: Automates time-consuming administrative tasks such as hardware provisioning, database setup, automated backups, point-in-time recovery, security patching, and multi-AZ failover for high availability.
rds.architectureRole: Stores relational structured application data, queried directly by ECS containers and Lambda backend functions.

sqs.title: Amazon SQS (Simple Queue Service)
sqs.summary: Fully managed message queuing service enabling decoupling and independent scaling of distributed services.
sqs.details:
SQS eliminates complexity associated with managing messaging middleware. It handles asynchronous job buffering with dead-letter queues (DLQs) for fault tolerance.

• Standard Queues: Nearly unlimited throughput with best-effort ordering and at-least-once delivery.
• FIFO Queues: Guaranteed first-in-first-out ordering and exactly-once processing.
sqs.architectureRole: Buffers background and long-running requests from ECS or API Gateway to be consumed asynchronously by worker Lambda functions.

lambda.title: AWS Lambda
lambda.summary: Zero-server compute service that runs your application code in response to events and automatically scales to demand.
lambda.details:
Lambda executes code only when triggered, charging only for the compute time consumed in milliseconds. In this architecture, Lambda serves two crucial roles:
1. Event-driven post-processing (e.g. triggered automatically when a user uploads an object to S3).
2. Asynchronous task execution consuming queued messages from SQS for operations taking 5–15 minutes.
lambda.architectureRole: Triggered by S3 upload events and SQS queue items to process data and send notification alerts via SES or WebSockets.

ses.title: Amazon SES (Simple Email Service)
ses.summary: Cost-effective, high-deliverability email service for sending transactional, operational, and marketing emails.
ses.details: Provides dedicated IP options, DKIM/SPF reputation tracking, deliverability dashboards, and bounce/complaint handling to ensure communications reach user inboxes reliably.
ses.architectureRole: Dispatched by worker Lambdas to send task completion emails, account confirmations, and transactional receipts.

elasticache.title: Amazon ElastiCache
elasticache.summary: Ultra-fast, fully managed in-memory data store supporting Redis and Memcached for microsecond response times.
elasticache.details: Greatly accelerates read-heavy workloads and reduces database load by caching frequently requested database queries, user session states, rate limits, and real-time leaderboards.
elasticache.architectureRole: Caches hot data for ECS and Lambda to offload repetitive read queries from Amazon RDS.

sns.title: Amazon SNS (Simple Notification Service)
sns.summary: Fully managed pub/sub messaging service for high-throughput, fan-out event distribution.
sns.details: Publishers send messages to an SNS topic, and subscribers (Amazon SQS queues, AWS Lambda functions, HTTP endpoints, mobile push, and SMS) automatically receive immediate copies.
sns.architectureRole: Fans out system events and status changes to multiple consumers, queues, and external webhook notification targets.

elasticache_sns.title: In-Memory Cache & Pub/Sub (ElastiCache / SNS)
elasticache_sns.summary: Combined caching and event distribution cluster managing state speed and real-time event dissemination.
elasticache_sns.details: This composite cluster provides both microsecond caching with ElastiCache (Redis) and event fan-out with SNS. In contrast to WebSockets, this pattern allows internal services to broadcast state updates across clusters.
elasticache_sns.architectureRole: Provides caching for database query offloading alongside pub/sub event broadcasting for internal microservices.

cloudfront.title: Amazon CloudFront (CDN)
cloudfront.summary: Global Content Delivery Network (CDN) delivering data, videos, APIs, and static assets with low latency and high speed.
cloudfront.details: CloudFront routes traffic to the nearest global Point of Presence (Edge Location). It securely terminates TLS/SSL at the edge, compresses assets, and caches S3 static content and web applications worldwide.
cloudfront.architectureRole: Distributes static web frontend assets cached from Amazon S3 and proxies dynamic API traffic toward the load balancer.

s3.title: Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service)
s3.summary: Industry-leading object storage designed for 99.999999999% (11 9's) data durability and unlimited scalability.
s3.details:
Stores files, images, documents, backups, and static website assets.

• Pre-Signed URLs: Allows clients to securely upload directly (Pre-Signed POST) or download (Pre-Signed GET) without routing heavy binary payloads through application servers.
s3.architectureRole: Stores user file uploads directly via Pre-Signed URLs and triggers worker Lambdas automatically upon file landing.

cloudwatch.title: Amazon CloudWatch
cloudwatch.summary: Centralized observability, logging, metrics collection, and alerting service for AWS resources and cloud workloads.
cloudwatch.details: Aggregates logs from ECS containers, Lambda runs, API Gateway, and RDS. Generates alarms based on metric thresholds (CPU, memory, HTTP 5xx errors) and triggers auto-scaling or incident notifications.
cloudwatch.architectureRole: Monitors health metrics across all infrastructure and collects container & serverless logs for debugging and auditing.

route53.title: Amazon Route 53
route53.summary: Highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service running on a global anycast network.
route53.details: Translates human-readable names (e.g., example.com) into numeric IP addresses. Provides health checks, latency-based routing, geo-DNS routing, and alias records to CloudFront and Application Load Balancers.
route53.architectureRole: Top-level DNS resolving user domain queries and pointing directly to CloudFront or external CDN edge distributions.

acm.title: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
acm.summary: Service that provisions, manages, and automatically renews public and private SSL/TLS certificates.
acm.details: Provides free public TLS certificates for use with AWS services like CloudFront, API Gateway, and Application Load Balancers, with zero-touch automatic DNS validation and renewals.
acm.architectureRole: Secures all inbound HTTPS connections by binding validated TLS certificates to CloudFront and Application Load Balancers.

elb.title: AWS Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
elb.summary: Automatically distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets and Availability Zones.
elb.details: Ensures high fault tolerance by continuously health-checking backend instances/containers and routing requests only to healthy targets.
elb.architectureRole: Distributes incoming traffic across backend container clusters running in multiple Availability Zones.

alb.title: Application Load Balancer (ALB)
alb.summary: Feature-rich Layer 7 load balancer routing HTTP/HTTPS traffic based on advanced request content attributes.
alb.details: Supports path-based routing (/api/* vs /static/*), host-based routing, WebSocket protocol routing, TLS termination, and direct integration with Amazon ECS container dynamic port mappings.
alb.architectureRole: Receives decrypted traffic from CloudFront/ACM and routes REST API requests to healthy ECS container tasks.

elb_alb.title: Elastic Load Balancing (ELB / ALB)
elb_alb.summary: Scalable traffic ingress balancing Layer 7 requests across redundant container instances and microservices.
elb_alb.details: Combines Application Load Balancers with target groups to handle health checking, TLS termination, and traffic distribution to backend ECS containers across multiple availability zones.
elb_alb.architectureRole: Acts as the single entry point for API traffic reaching the backend container infrastructure.

iam.title: AWS IAM (Identity and Access Management)
iam.summary: Fine-grained permission management controlling authentication and authorization for users, services, and workloads.
iam.details: Enforces the principle of least privilege. Uses IAM Roles with temporary credentials for ECS tasks and Lambda functions, avoiding hard-coded AWS access keys in source code.
iam.architectureRole: Grants granular permissions allowing ECS containers and Lambda functions to securely access S3, RDS, SQS, and CloudWatch.

parameter_store.title: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
parameter_store.summary: Secure, hierarchical storage for configuration data management and password/secret storage.
parameter_store.details: Stores environment variables, API tokens, database connection strings, and license keys. Encrypted with AWS KMS and integrated directly into ECS task definition environment injection.
parameter_store.architectureRole: Supplies encrypted database passwords and API configuration keys to containers and Lambda workers on boot.

opensearch.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service
opensearch.summary: Managed search and analytics engine derived from Elasticsearch for full-text search, filtering, and log analytics.
opensearch.details: Enables sub-second search queries across millions of records with autocomplete, fuzzy matching, faceted filtering, geospatial queries, and vector similarity search.
opensearch.architectureRole: Powers high-speed application search queries and real-time log exploration alongside the primary relational database.

api_gateway.title: Amazon API Gateway (V2 WebSocket / HTTP)
api_gateway.summary: Fully managed API hosting service supporting real-time two-way WebSocket connections and HTTP APIs.
api_gateway.details:
Maintains persistent, stateful WebSocket connections with client devices. When long-running tasks finish, backend workers broadcast immediate notifications back to users without requiring client polling.

• Cheaper & simpler than traditional custom-built WebSocket clusters running on continuous EC2 instances.
api_gateway.architectureRole: Maintains active WebSocket links with clients to push notifications when asynchronous tasks (5–15 min) finish.

cloudflare.title: Cloudflare
cloudflare.summary: Global CDN, DNS, and DDoS protection layer positioned at the Internet perimeter before AWS origins.
cloudflare.details: Provides edge caching, Web Application Firewall (WAF) rule sets, bot management, and SSL termination before routing legitimate traffic to AWS CloudFront or Route 53.
cloudflare.architectureRole: Acts as the outermost internet security shield and DNS proxy guarding the architecture against malicious traffic.

user.title: End User / Web Client
user.summary: End-user web browser or mobile client initiating HTTP requests, WebSocket streams, and file transfers.
user.details: Clients fetch the static UI from CloudFront, connect to API Gateway via WebSockets for real-time progress updates, and upload files directly to Amazon S3 via Pre-Signed POST URLs without loading application servers.
user.architectureRole: Interacts with CloudFront for assets, API Gateway for live WebSocket alerts, and S3 for direct file uploads.

admin.title: Administrator Client
admin.summary: System administrator or staff member accessing administrative panels, metrics dashboards, and configuration tools.
admin.details: Admins access operational views, monitor CloudWatch metrics, inspect OpenSearch analytics, and manage application configurations stored in Parameter Store.
admin.architectureRole: Consumes administrative APIs and observability dashboards to monitor system health and perform operational duties.
